messages:
Sam: Quick q — can we land on a compact set of rules for 4xx vs 5xx on /v1/generate (streaming + non-stream)? I sketched a proposal in the PR but want a short consensus before I ship.
Laura: +1 to standard: 4xx = client-side validation / contract issues; 5xx = server/runtime/inference failures. But streaming has edgecases (midstream validation vs runtime OOM).
Mike: For streaming: if we detect client validation before producing tokens -> 4xx and close. If failure happens after some tokens emitted -> return a final error event with 5xx and include partial=true in the body/metadata. Do not flip to 4xx midstream.
Emily: From product/UX: important to indicate whether results are partial and whether retry is safe. We should surface a retryable flag so SDKs can decide to continue or surface to users.
Sam: OK. What should the actual JSON error envelope look like? I want a tiny, stable shape so clients can parse efficiently.
Laura: Suggestion (minimal):
```
{ "error": {
    "type": "validation|quota|inference|internal",
    "code": "STRING_CODE",
    "message": "human readable",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```
Add HTTP status for routing but keep fields small.
Mike: For streaming SSE/CHUNK responses embed a terminal event like:
```
event: error
data: {"error": {"type":"inference","code":"MODEL_OOM","message":"out of memory","retryable":true}, "partial": true}
```
Then follow with connection close. That lets clients know they received partial tokens and whether to retry.
Laura: +1 to including partial: true. Also we should standardize codes (MODEL_OOM, INVALID_PROMPT, RATE_LIMIT, CONTRACT_MISMATCH).
Emily: Can we also add guidance for Retry-After and idempotency? e.g., if retryable=true and we return 429/503 include Retry-After header when possible.
Sam: Agreed. For idempotency: request-id or idempotency-key header. If clients supply idempotency-key we should guarantee dedup for a short window and return 409 if conflict?
Mike: I'd keep 409 for idempotency conflicts. And use 5xx for transient infra (503) with Retry-After when we know. 4xx: 400/413/422 depending on spec: 413 for prompt too large, 422 for schema mismatch.
Laura: One more nuance: when a user sends invalid function spec or tools list in the chat function call — treat as 4xx validation and include which field failed (path) to help debugging.
Sam: Nice. Who wants to own adding the schema & examples to the API spec and the SDK parsing? I'll attach a quick PR link.
Laura: I can do the spec + examples in openapi. Assign to me.
Mike: I'll update runtime to emit the streaming error event shape and ensure kernel OOM maps to MODEL_OOM.
Emily: I'll update the UX docs for partial results and recommended retry messaging.
CI-bot: deploy-check: PR #2761 has failing tests on python-sdk CI — please wait on merging until green :gear:
Sam: Noted. Laura, can you drop your PR link here when ready? I'll hold off merging until CI and runtime changes coordinate.
Laura: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/2789 — contains OpenAPI examples + error code table.
Mike: Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/441 (streaming error event + MODEL_OOM mapping). Tests mostly passing, a few flakies left.
Sam: Action items: 1) Laura add OpenAPI + example responses (owned) 2) Mike runtime streaming event + mapping (owned) 3) Emily product wording (owned) 4) Sam to update SDK guidance after both merged. I'll do a follow-up review tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Emily: One last callout — log the error.type and code in traces so customers can filter (incidents + cost monitoring). Small ask but useful.
Mike: Will wire that into tracing. Also adding metrics for midstream error rate.
Sam: Great. If no objections I'll mark this as the canonical guidance and add to the error-handling doc. Anyone opposed?
Laura: no objections.
Mike: looks good.
Emily: thumbs up.
Sam: Cool, closing thread — will post link to consolidated doc later.
